meta.method: nes-emu per-frame capture; each layer identified by exact pixel match against the extracted PNGs
meta.frameBasis: t=0 is the first non-black frame of the prison scene (absolute emulator frame 506). The black frames before it belong to rm_title's own fade-out, so in GMS the cutscene starts at t=0 with the scene already loaded.
meta.verified: background composite (panorama + fence) = 0 px mismatch at t=800; blimp sprite = 494/494 px exact at every sampled frame t=300/360/400/460 (dark) and t=540..740 (lit); whole-frame replay verifyAll over t=113..790 = 290/678 pixel-perfect with residual confined to a single 1-px edge column (NES 8-sprite/scanline clipping artefact, not reproducible)

fadeIn.measured: mean luminance 206.3 / 235.8 / 255.2 at 4-frame spacing, i.e. 80.8% / 92.4% / 100% of full brightness
fadeIn.note: alpha is of a BLACK overlay, 4 frames per step, then 0

top.note: single pan 0->256 over 256 frames, then frozen at 256 (shows the RIGHT half). Never wraps.

bottom.note: 2 px/frame, wraps every 256 px, travels exactly 512 px (2 laps) then stops back on offset 0 and stays.

x.note: 0.5 px/frame, x=8 at t=113, x=118 at t=332

prop.warning: the naive mapping (p==0 -> _0) is INVERTED - it is 180 deg out of phase

lit.note: lights up one frame after the beams start

beams.drawMode: OPAQUE full-sky replacement (not alpha-blended) - Part A backgrounds have 0 transparent pixels
beams.drawOrder: after the sky layer, before the fence; the blimp is drawn ABOVE the beams
beams.note: beams_0 best-aligns to the panorama at scroll offset 256 (5728/45056 px differ, the rest is the beam itself)

mute.note: hardware stops all sound before the fade-out; this cuts the 11th alarm

partAToPartBTransition.status: MEASURED - per-frame luminance + OAM sprite count from the ROM

absoluteFrames.1057-1065: lum  0.0  OAM cleared, 0 sprites  (blank hold, 9 frames)
absoluteFrames.1066-1071: lum  0.0  8 sprites present, still black  (6 frames)

model.anchor: pb_t = 0 at absolute frame 1066 (the frame Part B sprites load)

partAToPartBTransition.note: Part A's 1057-1065 is visually identical black, so the room_goto can sit at 1066 without any visible difference; this makes Part B's pb_t=0 line up exactly with the original.
